Bill.BriefDescription: Improving the quality and value of health care with greater transparency of price and quality data.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to improving the quality and value of health carewith greater transparency of price and quality data; and adding a newchapter to Title 48 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds there is significantvariation in health care with regard to price, quality, and value.Large purchasers, major companies purchasing health care includinglarge public purchasers, are demanding more tools that will assist themin controlling costs and increasing quality. Additional pricetransparency from health care providers and insurance carriers canassist purchasers in identifying variation in price and quality, andpurchasing for value.

The definitions in this section applythroughout this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Health insuring entity" or "insuring entity" means any partythat is by law, rule, policy, contract, or agreement legallyresponsible for payment of a claim for a health care service including,but not limited to: p. 1 SB 5537 (a) An insurance company providing disability insurance underchapter 48.20 or 48.21 RCW; (b) A health care service contractor providing health care coverageunder chapter 48.44 RCW; (c) A health maintenance organization providing comprehensivehealth care services under chapter 48.46 RCW; (d) An employer or union selfinsured plan; (e) Any private insurer, a group health plan, or a service benefitplan; (f) A managed care organization; (g) A pharmacy benefit manager; and (h) A thirdparty administrator. (2) "Health plan" or "plan" means any policy, contract, oragreement offered by an insuring entity to provide, arrange, reimburse,or pay for health care services except the following: (a) Longterm care insurance governed by chapter 48.84 or 48.83RCW; (b) Coverage supplemental to the coverage provided under 10 U.S.C.chapter 55; (c) Disability income; (d) Coverage incidental to a property/casualty liability insurancepolicy such as automobile personal injury protection coverage andhomeowner guest medical; (e) Workers' compensation coverage; (f) Accident only coverage; (g) Specified disease or illnesstriggered fixed payment insurance,hospital confinement fixed payment insurance, or other fixed paymentinsurance offered as an independent, noncoordinated benefit; and (h) Plans certified by the insurance commissioner in writing to: (i) Have a shortterm limited purpose or duration; or (ii) Be a guaranteed renewable studentonly plan available to acovered person while the covered person is enrolled as a regular fulltime undergraduate or graduate student at an accredited highereducation institution. (3) "Health plan statistical agent" or "statistical agent" means anentity the commissioner has designated to collect health carerelatedstatistical data from insuring entities and report the data to thecommissioner on behalf of those insuring entities. SB 5537 p. 2 (4) "Statistical plan" means a system for collecting informationfrom insuring entities.

(1) All health insuring entities must submitprice and quality data to the commissioner and to large grouppurchasers that includes the information for each provider andfacility. Contracts with providers and facilities must include arequirement that allows the release of price and quality information tothe commissioner and to the purchasers of the group coverage. (2) The commissioner must adopt rules to clarify the required dataand format for submission. The types of data must include at aminimum: Health care claims and enrollment data; paid health careclaims data; and data related to costs, prices, quality, andutilization. (3) The rules must establish criteria and procedures for thedevelopment of limited use data sets, and criteria and procedures toensure that limited use data sets are accessible and compliant withfederal and state privacy laws. (4) The rules must ensure that data reported to the commissionermay only be disclosed in a form and manner that ensures the privacy andsecurity of personal health information as required by state andfederal laws. The collection, storage, and release of health care dataand other information under this section is subject to the requirementsof the federal health insurance portability and accountability act. (5) The commissioner may choose to designate a health planstatistical agent responsible for collection, auditing, preparation,and reporting of the health carerelated data and information. (a) If the commissioner chooses to designate a statistical agent tobe responsible for the data, the commissioner must adopt rules for thestatistical agent to use when collecting and reporting health planstatistical data. (b) Rules adopted under this chapter must be consistent withstandards adopted by the accredited standards committee X12 of theAmerican national standards institute, the centers for medicare andmedicaid services, and the national council for prescription drugprograms. At a minimum, these rules must establish the time, place,form, and manner of reporting data under this chapter, including: (i) Requiring the use of unique patient and provider identifiers; p. 3 SB 5537 (ii) Specifying a uniform coding system that reflects all healthcare utilization and costs for health care services provided toWashington residents; (iii) Establishing enrollment thresholds below which reporting willbe voluntary; and (iv) Establishing the types of data insuring entities must reportunder this chapter, including: (A) Health care claims and enrollment data; (B) Paid health care claims data; (C) Data related to race, ethnicity, and primary language collectedin a manner consistent with established national standards; and (D) Any other data or statistics related to health care costs,prices, quality, utilization, or resources that the commissioner needsto carry out the purposes of this chapter.

Health insuring entities must report dataidentified by this chapter and by the commissioner by rule undersection 3 of this act. Each insuring entity insurer must: (1) Report its insurance statistical data to the commissioner orthe statistical agent designated by the commissioner; (2) Comply with the reporting requirements and data qualityprocedures published in rule; and (3) Adopt edit and audit procedures to screen and check data forreasonableness and accuracy.

(1) Any insuring entity that fails to reportas required in this chapter or rules adopted by the commissioner may besubject to a civil penalty. (2) The commissioner must adopt a schedule of penalties not toexceed five hundred dollars per day per violation, as determined by theseverity of the violation. (3) Civil penalties imposed under this section may be remitted ormitigated by the commissioner if the terms and conditions areconsistent with the public health and safety. (4) Civil penalties incurred under any law of this state are notallowable as costs for the purpose of rate determination or forreimbursement by a thirdparty payer.
Sections 1 through 5 of this act constitutea new chapter in Title 48 RCW.
